answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a bonded identity deposit: each identity must lock a modest, refundable stake before it can earn, and the stake is returned only after a period of honest work. If two identities are caught sharing the same work, keys, or payment trail, both bonds are slashed, so a fraud ring ends with a hollow return. A nebula of cheap fake accounts therefore costs one full bond per fake, while the tide of rewards flows only to identities whose deposits remain intact, so creating thousands of sybils multiplies cost without multiplying reward.
